content.value_statement: React TypeScript work slows down when events, hooks, and routing types are unclear. This skill gives proven patterns for React 18-19 components, hooks, Server Components, and routers.
actual_capabilities: Provides typed component prop patterns using native element extensions and discriminated unions.
Shows event handler types for forms, inputs, keyboard, mouse, focus, clipboard, and drag events.
Documents React 19 patterns including ref as prop, useActionState, use(), and Server Components.
Gives reusable generic component patterns for tables, lists, modals, selects, and form fields.
Explains type-safe routing with TanStack Router and React Router v7 loaders, params, and search values.
Guides custom hook typing with useState, useRef, useReducer, useContext, and tuple returns.
limitations: It is focused on React with TypeScript and does not cover plain JavaScript React projects.
It does not provide automated tests, build scripts, or runnable scaffolding commands.
Router guidance is limited to TanStack Router and React Router v7 patterns.
React Native and non-React TypeScript patterns are outside its documented scope.

use_cases.title: Ship Typed UI Components
use_cases.description: Create buttons, forms, tables, and reusable components with accurate props and safer event handling.

use_cases.title: Standardize Design System Types
use_cases.description: Apply consistent patterns for native element props, render props, variants, refs, and generic component APIs.

use_cases.title: Adopt Modern React Routing
use_cases.description: Use documented loader, action, params, and search parameter patterns for typed application routes.

prompt_templates.title: Create Typed Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a React TypeScript component for [component name]. Include native element props, typed children, and clear variant props.

prompt_templates.title: Type Event Handlers
prompt_templates.prompt: Type the event handlers for this React form. Cover submit, input change, keyboard handling, and currentTarget access.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate React 19 Patterns
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this React component for React 19 compatibility. Replace deprecated ref and form patterns with current typed patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Design Typed Routing
prompt_templates.prompt: Design type-safe routes for this React app using [TanStack Router or React Router v7]. Include params, search values, loaders, and actions.

output_examples.input: Type an input change handler for a search box.
output_examples.output: Returns the correct React change event type, explains safe currentTarget usage, and notes where validation should run.

output_examples.input: Create a generic table for user records.
output_examples.output: Provides a typed table design with inferred column keys, render value guidance, and a stable key extraction pattern.

output_examples.input: Move a form to React 19 Server Actions.
output_examples.output: Describes the server action boundary, client form state pattern, pending state handling, and cache revalidation points.

best_practices: Use specific React event types so currentTarget and target have useful TypeScript inference.
Use discriminated unions and native element prop extensions for safer component APIs.
Load reference sections only when deeper routing, hook, or Server Component guidance is needed.
anti_patterns: Do not use any for event handlers when a specific React event type exists.
Do not use deprecated React 19 patterns such as forwardRef for new ref handling.
Do not mix Server Component and Client Component responsibilities in the same file.

faq.question: What React versions does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers React 18 and React 19, with specific guidance for React 19 APIs and migrations.

faq.question: Does it generate complete applications?
faq.answer: No. It provides typed patterns and examples that can be applied inside an existing React project.

faq.question: Can it help with event handler typing?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes patterns for mouse, form, input, keyboard, focus, clipboard, drag, touch, and wheel events.

faq.question: Which routers are documented?
faq.answer: It documents TanStack Router and React Router v7 patterns for params, search values, loaders, and actions.

faq.question: Does it run scripts or install dependencies?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation-only and does not include executable scripts or install commands.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible workflows.
